extracted.intended_audience: journalism educators, composition instructors, and education researchers
extracted.subtask_short: perception study: composition to news writing
extracted.subtask_description: A small-sample survey research report examining journalism students' perceptions of freshman English composition as preparation for news writing and testing which variables best predict success in introductory journalism courses. Includes analysis of survey responses and predictors across two universities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perceived usefulness of freshman composition as preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalism students perceived that freshman composition did not provide a good foundation for them in other courses and in the work world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as Result (1) of the 17-item survey administered to 77 students at South Dakota State University and Southwest Missouri State University; finding summarized from students' self-reports about transferability of composition course skills to academic and workplace contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overlap (or difference) in writing skills emphasized by composition vs. journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Freshman composition and journalism emphasize different writing skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as Result (2); the survey asked students whether the two courses emphasized the same writing skills, and responses indicated perceived differences in skill focus between the composition course and the introductory news writing course.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predictor variables for success in introductory news writing
rubrics_metrics.description: English American College Testing (ACT) score, composite ACT score, and gender were better predictors of student's success in introductory journalism classes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as Result (3); the study compared freshman composition grade against other variables (ACT scores, gender) to determine which were stronger predictors of performance in the introductory journalism course.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of a 17-item survey instrument to evaluate perceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Subjects responded to a 17-item survey concerning the two courses (freshman composition and introductory journalism).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methodological detail: 77 students who had just completed both courses at two universities completed the survey; eleven tables of data and 31 references accompany the report. The survey items formed the basis for measuring perceptions and comparing course emphases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome operationalization: 'success' in introductory journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: The study uses students' performance in the introductory news writing course as the outcome measure of interest when assessing predictors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit criterion: 'success' in the journalism course is the dependent variable contrasted with predictors like composition grade, ACT scores, and gender; exact operational definition (grade thresholds or measures) is reported in the full text/tables.
